entities.summary: Prince Paul II Anton Esterházy de Galántha (1711-04-22, Eisenstadt - 1762-03-18) was a Hungarian prince, soldier, and patron of music from the Esterházy family, who played a crucial role in shaping the musical landscape of Eastern Europe during the Early Modern period. Born into a powerful noble family, Paul II Anton was educated in music and philosophy, and he became a prominent figure in the development of classical music, commissioning works by renowned composers such as Haydn and Mozart. His patronage of the arts helped to establish Vienna as a center of musical excellence, which had a lasting impact on the development of classical music. Paul II Anton's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his patronage of the arts helped to lay the foundations for the musical achievements of future generations. The Esterházy family's musical patronage was also marked by a distinctive blend of Baroque and Classical styles, which continues to influence musical tastes to this day. As a soldier, Paul II Anton fought in several battles, including the War of the Austrian Succession, and his military service helped to secure the Esterházy family's position as one of the most powerful noble families in Hungary. Through his military service and patronage of the arts, Paul II Anton played a significant role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of Eastern Europe during the 18th century.
